During **2026-10-10 18:00–18:15 UTC**, a single US host **`198.51.100.10`** running the **Artillery load-testing tool** directed a sustained single-source HTTP flood at `d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net` — **~34,000 requests in 15 minutes** (~35–40 req/s), far above the WAF rate rule's 300-req/5-min per-IP limit. It was benign in content (normal e-commerce paths, no SQLi/XSS/bad-input patterns) — a volumetric flood, not an exploitation attempt. The burst briefly overwhelmed the origin (**~35% 5xx errors for one minute at 18:05–18:06**), which then self-recovered. BytesDownloaded stayed normal, so there was no data exfiltration.

**Was it stopped? No.** WAF *detected* the abuse — the rate-based rule `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront` counted the over-limit IP ~32,057 times — but took no action because it is configured in **Count (detect-only) mode**. No managed rule group blocked or challenged the traffic (ALLOW ≈ 33,972; BLOCK = 2 unrelated; CHALLENGE/CAPTCHA = 0). The flood passed through end-to-end, exactly as the alert `e4-detected-not-blocked-rate-rule` name states.

**Root cause:** the rate-based rule's action is `Count` rather than `Block` — a deterministic configuration gap, meaning an identical flood would again pass unimpeded.

The mitigation plan (switch the rule from Count to Block, gated on confirming the load-test traffic is unwanted, with full backup/rollback) is available as its own artifact. Nothing further remains to investigate.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Over-limit IP detected by rate rule but not blocked
**Description:** The rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront detected IP 198.51.100.10 massively exceeding its per-IP limit of 300 req/300s (~32,057 non-terminating COUNT matches in the window; log rateBasedRuleList names the IP with maxRateAllowed 300), but did not block or challenge it — action=ALLOW end-to-end. This is precisely the alert condition e4-detected-not-blocked-rate-rule.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T18:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

### Momentary origin 5xx spike during request burst
**Description:** At 2026-10-10 18:06 UTC a single-minute burst reached 3,873 requests (~1.5x baseline peak) and the origin returned 34.86% 5xx for that minute; BytesDownloaded stayed normal and errors recovered immediately. Driven by load-test traffic from 198.51.100.10 that WAF allowed through.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T18:06:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:07:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Rate-based rule in Count mode, not Block
**Description:** WAF S3 logs confirm the mechanism: the rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront matched source IP 198.51.100.10 (country US, user-agent "Artillery (https://artillery.io)" — a load-testing tool) with action=COUNT (non-terminating). The request terminated on terminatingRuleId=Default_Action with action=ALLOW; no managed rule group (CommonRuleSet, KnownBadInputs, SQLi, IpReputation, AntiDDoS) blocked it. This directly explains the alert "e4-detected-not-blocked-rate-rule": because the rule is in Count mode, WAF detected the IP exceeding the 300 req/5min limit but did not block it. Not yet promoted — the investigation is still synthesizing WAF logs and metrics.
**Cascades to:** symptom-detected-not-blocked, symptom-origin-5xx

### Root Cause: Rate-based rule set to Count instead of Block
**Description:** AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront (300 req / 300s per IP) is configured with Action: Count, so it only tags over-limit traffic and never blocks it. This is the fundamental cause: any single IP exceeding the limit will be detected-but-not-blocked, exactly as the alert reports. Switching the rule to Block (and/or enabling the AntiDDoS challenge action, which currently flags challengeable requests but issues zero challenges) would stop recurrence.
**Cascades to:** finding-count-mode, symptom-detected-not-blocked, symptom-origin-5xx

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Change the WAFv2 rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront (Priority 1) from Action=Count to Action=Block on WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, so any single IP exceeding 300 requests / 300s is actively blocked rather than only counted. Gated on first confirming the flood traffic is unwanted.

## Reasoning
During 2026-10-10 18:00–18:15 UTC a single host (198.51.100.10, UA 'Artillery') sent ~34,000 requests at CloudFront distribution EEXAMPLE000001, briefly overwhelming the origin (~35% 5xx for one minute at 18:05–18:06) before self-recovering. The rate-based rule detected the abuse (~32,057 non-terminating COUNT matches) but took no action because it is in Count (detect-only) mode. Switching it to Block closes the gap source-agnostically. A static IP block of 198.51.100.10 was intentionally NOT proposed (brittle stopgap superseded by the rate-based Block); the AntiDDoS Challenge action is already ENABLED, so no change is needed there.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Capture the current WebACL (Rules, DefaultAction, VisibilityConfig…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 > waf-backup-pre-change.json
```
**Purpose:** Capture the current WebACL (Rules, DefaultAction, VisibilityConfig, LockToken) as the rollback baseline; documents that the rate rule is currently Action=Count.
**Advisory:** Confirm the saved backup is for the correct WebACL (CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, Id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4, CLOUDFRONT scope) before relying on it for rollback.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Gate the change on confirmation that the flood is unwanted, preventing…
**Type:** text
Confirm with the application / load-test owner that traffic from 198.51.100.10 (UA 'Artillery') is unwanted and NOT an authorized load test. This is a demo/test distribution; do NOT proceed with Block if the traffic is an authorized/scheduled load test.
**Purpose:** Gate the change on confirmation that the flood is unwanted, preventing blocking of legitimate authorized testing.
**Risks:** If the traffic is an authorized load test, enabling Block would throttle intended testing. Only proceed once ownership confirms the traffic is unwanted.

#### 2.2 Fetch the current WebACL and a fresh LockToken immediately before the…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Fetch the current WebACL and a fresh LockToken immediately before the change; confirm the rate rule still has Action=Count.
**Risks:** The LockToken changes on every write; a stale token causes WAFOptimisticLockException. Always use the token from this fresh read.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Change AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront Action from…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --default-action Allow={} --lock-token <FRESH_LOCK_TOKEN_FROM_PRE_VALIDATE> --visibility-config SampledRequestsEnabled=true,CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true,MetricName=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --rules <FULL_RULES_ARRAY_WITH_RATE_RULE_ACTION_SET_TO_Block>
```
**Purpose:** Change AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront Action from {Count:{}} to {Block:{}}. Resubmit the entire Rules array unchanged except that one action; preserve all other rules, priorities, OverrideActions, Statements and VisibilityConfig; use the fresh LockToken. Recommended to use --cli-input-json to resubmit the full array accurately.
**Risks:** Once Block is active, any single IP exceeding 300 req / 300s is blocked; a legitimate client or shared NAT/proxy that bursts above the threshold could be temporarily blocked. The 300 limit is unchanged — only enforcement behavior changes., Submitting an incomplete Rules array would drop other protective rules; the array from pre_validate must be resubmitted in full.
**Advisory:** The AntiDDoS Challenge action is already ENABLED in this WebACL; no change to it is included or required.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm the rate-based rule action is now Block and other rules remain…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --query "WebACL.Rules[?Name=='AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront'].Action"
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the rate-based rule action is now Block and other rules remain unchanged.

#### 4.2 Monitor that over-limit requests are now being blocked by the…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/WAFV2 --metric-name BlockedRequests --dimensions Name=WebACL,Value=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 Name=Rule,Value=AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront Name=Region,Value=CloudFront --start-time 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z --end-time 2026-10-10T19:00:00Z --period 300 --statistics Sum --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Monitor that over-limit requests are now being blocked by the rate-based rule.
**Advisory:** If no over-limit traffic is occurring, BlockedRequests may legitimately be zero; this metric confirms enforcement only when a source exceeds the 300-request threshold.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Revert the rate-based rule to Count if Block causes unintended impact
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --default-action Allow={} --lock-token <FRESH_LOCK_TOKEN> --visibility-config SampledRequestsEnabled=true,CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true,MetricName=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --rules <FULL_RULES_ARRAY_FROM_BACKUP_WITH_RATE_RULE_ACTION_SET_TO_Count>
```
**Purpose:** Revert the rate-based rule to Count if Block causes unintended impact. Fetch a fresh LockToken first, then resubmit the backup Rules array with the rule Action set back to {Count:{}}, leaving all other rules unchanged.
**Risks:** Reverting to Count restores detect-only behavior, re-opening the original gap where floods are counted but not blocked.
**Advisory:** Use the backup captured in the prepare phase as the source of truth for the restored Rules array.
